site.name: pelagic
site.summary: pelagic-clone Marketing site (landing page) for the fictional open-source vector database Pelagic. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page landing: top nav + animated GitHub-stars counter pill; hero with title, dual CTAs, `pip install` copy strip, rotating benchmark numbers, right-side 4-language (Python / Node / Go / curl) code tabs; Trusted-by logo row; 3 core-feature cards; Ingest → Index → Query three-step flow; architecture SVG diagram; customer quote cards; left Blog 5 posts + right Changelog 5 entries dual feed; 4-column footer with sitemap | | `styles.css` | Brand color #0E5C8A deep-sea blue; Inter + JetBrains Mono; responsive at 3 breakpoints (>1100 / 880–1100 / <880) | | `script.js` | Stars-counter 1.2s eased animation; code tabs switch Python / Node / Go / curl; benchmark rows rotate every 2.5s; `pip install pelagic` copy toast; fictional-logo rendering |

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively validate the single-page landing experience of Pelagic, focusing on interactive components, dynamic animations, and responsive layout scaling.
run_plan.summary: The exploration will begin on desktop by interacting with custom JS components, notably the code snippet tabs and the copy-to-clipboard function. It will then verify internal navigation anchors and the rendering of complex content blocks like the architecture diagram and dual feeds. Finally, the run will switch to a mobile viewport to investigate flagged tap-target warnings and ensure the layout gracefully degrades.
assumptions: The site consists entirely of a single index.html page, so navigation links (Product, Docs, Pricing) likely rely on anchor scrolling or are placeholder links.
The 'copy install command' functionality should provide some visual feedback (like a toast) when clicked.
The code tabs (python, node, go, curl) toggle visibility of different text blocks within the same container without page reloads.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets on top navigation and code tabs, especially problematic on mobile.
Horizontal overflow or clipping of the code block on narrow viewports.
Stacking behavior of multi-column sections (features, customer quotes, footer) on mobile.
JS errors that might break the tab switching or copy functionality.

phases.title: Desktop Interactive Components
phases.objective: Validate JS-driven interactive elements like code tabs and the copy button.
key_checks: Click through 'node', 'go', and 'curl' tabs to ensure the code snippet text updates accordingly.
Click the 'Copy install command' button and observe UI for a success toast or state change.
exit_criteria: All four code tabs successfully display different content.
Copy button interaction is completed and recorded.

phases.title: Desktop Navigation & Layout Flow
phases.objective: Ensure header links work and content sections render correctly as the user scrolls.
key_checks: Click navigation links (Product, Docs, Pricing, Blog) to confirm anchor scrolling behavior.
Verify visibility of the Trusted-by logo row, architecture SVG, and dual Blog/Changelog feeds.
exit_criteria: Page scrolled to bottom, verifying all major content sections are visible and structured well.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Tap Targets
phases.objective: Evaluate mobile layout degradation and specifically test elements flagged for small tap targets.
key_checks: Verify if top navigation collapses into a hamburger menu or remains as small links.
Check if the hero section text and code block stack vertically without horizontal scrolling.
Attempt to tap the code language tabs (python, node, etc.) on mobile to assess usability.
Verify multi-column sections (features, footer) collapse to single columns.
exit_criteria: Mobile layout captured from top to bottom, with interaction attempts on the previously flagged small tap targets.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise code tabs, copy functionality, and anchor navigation.
coverage_targets.mobile: Validate layout breakpoints and re-test interactive tabs for usability.

notes: Pay attention to the rotating benchmark numbers and star counter animation during initial load; capture early screenshots if possible.

prescan_summary.visible_text_excerpt: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 17.8k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl from pelagic import Client db = Client("https://api.pelagic.dev", api_key="pk_live_…") index = db.create_index( name="docs", dim=1536, metric="cosine", hybrid=True, ) index.upsert([ {"id": "doc-001", "vector": embed(text), "filter": {"lang": "en"}} ]) hits = index.query( vector=embed("what is hnsw"), top_k=10, filter={"lang": "en"}, rerank="bge-large", ) 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION

observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl curl -X POST https://api.pelagic.dev/v1/indexes/docs/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_…" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "vector": [0.0123, -0.0876, ...], "top_k": 10, "filter": {"lang": "en"}, "rerank": "bge-large" }' 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Architecture Client SDKs py · node · go · rust Gateway auth · rate-limit · cache Coordinator routing · planner Shard 1 Shard 2 Shard 3 Object storage "We swapped our managed FAISS for self-hosted Pelagic in an afternoon. p95 fell from 91ms to 17ms, and we cut our retrieval bill by two-thirds. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Throughput: 42k QPS python node go curl curl -X POST https://api.pelagic.dev/v1/indexes/docs/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_…" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "vector": [0.0123, -0.0876, ...], "top_k": 10, "filter": {"lang": "en"}, "rerank": "bge-large" }' 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. observation.title: Pelagic — Open-source vector database
observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Throughput: 42k QPS python node go curl from pelagic import Client db = Client("https://api.pelagic.dev", api_key="pk_live_…") index = db.create_index( name="docs", dim=1536, metric="cosine", hybrid=True, ) index.upsert([ {"id": "doc-001", "vector": embed(text), "filter": {"lang": "en"}} ]) hits = index.query( vector=embed("what is hnsw"), top_k=10, filter={"lang": "en"}, rerank="bge-large", ) 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Index build: 2.3× faster python node go curl import { Pelagic } from "pelagic"; const db = new Pelagic({ apiKey: "pk_live_…" }); const index = await db.createIndex({ name: "docs", dim: 1536, metric: "cosine", hybrid: true, }); await index.upsert([ { id: "doc-001", vector: await embed(text), filter: { lang: "en" } }, ]); const hits = await index.query({ vector: await embed("what is hnsw"), topK: 10, filter: { lang: "en" }, rerank: "bge-large", }); 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. observation.title: Pelagic — Open-source vector database
observation.visible_text: Pelagic ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl curl -X POST https://api.pelagic.dev/v1/indexes/docs/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_…" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "vector": [0.0123, -0.0876, ...], "top_k": 10, "filter": {"lang": "en"}, "rerank": "bge-large" }' 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Architecture Client SDKs py · node · go · rust Gateway auth · rate-limit · cache Coordinator routing · planner Shard 1 Shard 2 Shard 3 Object storage "We swapped our managed FAISS for self-hosted Pelagic in an afternoon. p95 fell from 91ms to 17ms, and we cut our retrieval bill by two-thirds. The migration tool re-indexed 240M vectors without a single drop." SF Sana Falconer Staff ML Engineer, Halcyon Health From the blog 2026-05-04 Why we rewrote our HNSW build in Rust A 1,400-line memory-allocator rewrite cut index build time by 2.3× — the postmortem. Marisol Chen 2026-04-21 Pelagic 0.42: hybrid search, done right Dense + sparse + filter in a single planner. The query language, the plan, the numbers. Aditya Rao 2026-04-02 One billion vectors on a single $400/mo box Tuning IVF-PQ and disk caching for the long tail of recall. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. observation.title: Pelagic — Open-source vector database
observation.visible_text: Pelagic ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl curl -X POST https://api.pelagic.dev/v1/indexes/docs/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_…" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "vector": [0.0123, -0.0876, ...], "top_k": 10, "filter": {"lang": "en"}, "rerank": "bge-large" }' 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Architecture Client SDKs py · node · go · rust Gateway auth · rate-limit · cache Coordinator routing · planner Shard 1 Shard 2 Shard 3 Object storage "We swapped our managed FAISS for self-hosted Pelagic in an afternoon. p95 fell from 91ms to 17ms, and we cut our retrieval bill by two-thirds. The migration tool re-indexed 240M vectors without a single drop." SF Sana Falconer Staff ML Engineer, Halcyon Health From the blog 2026-05-04 Why we rewrote our HNSW build in Rust A 1,400-line memory-allocator rewrite cut index build time by 2.3× — the postmortem. Marisol Chen 2026-04-21 Pelagic 0.42: hybrid search, done right Dense + sparse + filter in a single planner. The query language, the plan, the numbers. Aditya Rao 2026-04-02 One billion vectors on a single $400/mo box Tuning IVF-PQ and disk caching for the long tail of recall. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. observation.title: Pelagic — Open-source vector database
observation.visible_text: Pelagic ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Index build: 2.3× faster python node go curl curl -X POST https://api.pelagic.dev/v1/indexes/docs/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_…" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "vector": [0.0123, -0.0876, ...], "top_k": 10, "filter": {"lang": "en"}, "rerank": "bge-large" }' 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Architecture Client SDKs py · node · go · rust Gateway auth · rate-limit · cache Coordinator routing · planner Shard 1 Shard 2 Shard 3 Object storage "We swapped our managed FAISS for self-hosted Pelagic in an afternoon. p95 fell from 91ms to 17ms, and we cut our retrieval bill by two-thirds. The migration tool re-indexed 240M vectors without a single drop." SF Sana Falconer Staff ML Engineer, Halcyon Health From the blog 2026-05-04 Why we rewrote our HNSW build in Rust A 1,400-line memory-allocator rewrite cut index build time by 2.3× — the postmortem. Marisol Chen 2026-04-21 Pelagic 0.42: hybrid search, done right Dense + sparse + filter in a single planner. The query language, the plan, the numbers. Aditya Rao 2026-04-02 One billion vectors on a single $400/mo box Tuning IVF-PQ and disk caching for the long tail of recall. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale.
